items.title: FCA and Bank of England set out shared vision for tokenisation in UK wholesale markets
items.summary: FCA and Bank of England set out shared vision for tokenisation and DLT adoption in UK wholesale markets, seeking industry views.
items.why_it_matters: Directly shapes the regulatory framework for tokenisation platforms and digital asset firms operating or planning to operate in UK markets.

items.title: FCA, Bank of England and Treasury joint statement on frontier AI models and cyber resilience
items.summary: FCA, Bank of England and Treasury issue joint statement warning that frontier AI models pose escalating cyber and operational resilience threats to firms.
items.why_it_matters: Every AI-native fintech and crypto firm must immediately assess cyber controls and operational resilience against frontier-AI-enabled attack vectors.

items.title: FCA opens doors to support fast-growing financial firms
items.summary: FCA's Scale-up Unit opens to solo-regulated firms offering tailored regulatory navigation support for fast-growing fintechs.
items.why_it_matters: Direct opportunity for fintech and crypto firms to engage the FCA proactively, reducing regulatory risk and accelerating product approvals.

items.title: Competition Act 1998 investigations
items.summary: FCA confirms Competition Act investigations into Mastercard, PayPal and Visa for suspected anti-competitive conduct in digital wallet funding.
items.why_it_matters: Fintechs and crypto payment firms relying on card network rails or competing with PayPal face material market structure and compliance risk.

items.title: Kevin Warsh takes oath of office as chairman and a member of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, and the Federal Open Market Committee unanimously selects Warsh as its chairman
items.summary: Kevin Warsh sworn in as Federal Reserve Chair and unanimously elected FOMC chairman.
items.why_it_matters: Leadership change at the Fed signals potential policy direction shifts on crypto, fintech oversight, and capital rules that CROs should monitor closely.

items.title: Our response to the Treasury’s policy statement on Consumer Credit Act reform
items.summary: FCA responds to Treasury's Consumer Credit Act 1974 reform, shifting toward flexible FCA-rules-based regime.
items.why_it_matters: Fintechs offering consumer credit or BNPL products should prepare for new FCA rulemaking replacing prescriptive CCA requirements.

items.title: ESMA issues guidance on effective use of resolution tools in CCP crisis planning
items.summary: ESMA issues guidance on effective use of resolution tools in central counterparty crisis planning.
items.why_it_matters: Crypto exchanges and DeFi platforms with CCP-like functions should monitor CCP resolution frameworks as regulatory analogies may be applied to them.

items.title: ESMA identifies areas for further supervisory convergence on compliance and internal audit in the funds sector
items.summary: ESMA identifies supervisory convergence priorities for compliance and internal audit functions within EU fund managers.
items.why_it_matters: Crypto funds and hedge funds operating under AIFMD in the EU should review compliance and internal audit frameworks against ESMA's benchmarks.

items.title: ESMA consults on a new simplified approach to updating MMF stress test parameters
items.summary: ESMA consults on simplified methodology for updating stress test parameters for money market funds.
items.why_it_matters: Stablecoin issuers and tokenised money market fund operators should monitor MMF stress test evolution as regulatory analogies are frequently drawn.

items.title: ESMA advances the simplification of EU reporting frameworks for funds and transactions
items.summary: ESMA proposes simplification of EU reporting frameworks for funds and transaction reporting obligations.
items.why_it_matters: Crypto funds and fintechs subject to EU reporting regimes could see material operational burden reduction if simplification proposals are adopted.

items.title: ESMA launches its sixth stress test exercise for Central Counterparties
items.summary: ESMA launches sixth CCP stress test exercise to assess resilience of EU central counterparties under adverse scenarios.
items.why_it_matters: Crypto trading platforms and firms with CCP exposures should assess counterparty risk implications of any stress test findings when published.

items.title: Decisions taken by the Governing Council of the ECB (in addition to decisions setting interest rates)
items.summary: ECB Governing Council publishes routine non-interest-rate decisions covering internal governance and operational matters.
items.why_it_matters: Unlikely to contain direct impact for frontier firms; worth a quick scan for any surprise prudential or market infrastructure decisions.

items.title: Agencies publish resolution plan feedback letters for certain domestic and foreign banking organizations
items.summary: US agencies release resolution plan feedback letters for domestic and foreign banking organizations.
items.why_it_matters: Primarily legacy bank-focused, but resolution planning expectations can migrate to systemic fintechs and large crypto platforms over time.

items.title: EBA E-mail alert 22 May, 2026
items.summary: EBA publishes its routine weekly email alert newsletter digest for 22 May 2026.
items.why_it_matters: Aggregated newsletter with no standalone regulatory substance; content within may be relevant but cannot be assessed from this entry.

items.title: A Modern Code for a Modernising Movement - Speech by Deputy Governor Colm Kincaid at ILCU
items.summary: Central Bank of Ireland deputy governor speech addresses modernisation of the Irish credit union regulatory code.
items.why_it_matters: Credit union specific and Ireland domestic; no material relevance to frontier finance firms or crypto and fintech sectors.
